subject: Press & logo use — proposed exceptions and next steps
messages:
From: Gavin Reed <gavin.reed@clearsky.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@clearsky.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW / MSA redlines (press & logo usage)

Thanks — attaching our redlines to the MSA and order form. A few highlights that are mandatory for us, and that we will not accept as written in the current draft: 

- Customer logo use: we cannot grant blanket logo license for placement across vendor marketing channels. Any logo use must be separately approved per instance and limited to a small set of pre-approved assets.
- Press releases: require mutual sign-off at least 30 days before publication; no embargo-broken exceptions.
- Reference rights: restricted to non-confidential, non-technical quotes and anonymized case studies unless we explicitly opt-in.
- Publicity exceptions for regulatory disclosures are fine (for example, required by a governmental authority) but should be limited.

We attached a redlined PDF (ClearSky_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) showing proposed language. If you can circulate a counterproposal that narrows the publicity and logo clauses, we can escalate internally. Our legal team (Elena) is on copy and available to coordinate.

Best,
Gavin
General Counsel
ClearSky AI

[Attachment: ClearSky_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Re: SOW / MSA redlines (press & logo usage)

Looping you both in — Gavin pushed back hard on the publicity/logo language in the MSA and wants very restrictive terms. Key asks from Clearsky: per-instance approval for logos, 30-day mutual sign-off on press, and reference rights limited to anonymized or short non-technical quotes.

Marissa — marketing has a planned joint announcement window the week of July 9th. If we can’t get logo permission, can we still run an anonymized case study + quote?

Neha — can you propose a compromise that preserves our ability to list customers and use logos in a controlled way? I attached the redlines from Gavin for reference.

I think we can trade a slightly longer sign-off window for a limited, pre-approved asset set and a short approval SLA (14 days) on our side. Please advise next steps and whether this needs escalation to legal leadership.

Thanks —

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FW: Re: SOW / MSA redlines (press & logo usage)

Thanks for the context and the redlines. I reviewed Gavin’s notes — below is a suggested compromise that balances ClearSky’s privacy concerns and our marketing needs: 

1) Logo use: allow placement of ClearSky logo on Redwood’s "Customer" page and in one-pager partner materials, provided each usage is pre-cleared through a single email approval containing the asset and intended placement. Approval SLA: 14 business days (we accept 14 rather than their 30 for operational practicality).

2) Press releases: mutual sign-off is reasonable. Propose 14 calendar days review for standard announcements, 30 calendar days for joint product launches or case study-level PR. We will accept a 30-day window for larger co-marketing, and 14 days for short public statements.

3) Reference rights: limit to non-confidential, non-technical quotes and anonymized case study text unless an explicit opt-in is provided. We should add language allowing Redwood to use anonymized performance metrics (rounded, aggregated) unless specifically restricted.

4) Approval mechanics: require customer to provide a single point of contact and to provide approvals via email thread. Include explicit attachment of the final press release or asset when approving.

5) If customer refuses logo use entirely, document an alternative: the right to publish an anonymized case study + approved quote.

I've drafted suggested clause language and attached it as Proposed_Press_Clause_redline.docx. This is our preferred starting point; if Cleasky wants different windows we can push an internal exec ask.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

[Attachment: Proposed_Press_Clause_redline.docx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FW: Re: SOW / MSA redlines (press & logo usage)

Appreciate the thoughtful compromise, Neha — this would work for marketing if we get either: (a) a pre-approved asset pack and permission to use the logo on the customer page + one promotional asset, or (b) permission for an anonymized case study plus a short quote from their CRO/Head of Product.

Campaign timing: we need a firm yes/no by June 26 to make creative and PR scheduling work for the July 9 window. If Clearsky insists on 30-day mandatory review for every release, we’ll miss that date.

If they hold the line, we should escalate to the deal sponsor (Rishi) to approve a concession (e.g., 30-day sign-off but with a guaranteed "priority review" lane for marquee launches).

Marissa Cole
Head of Marketing, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Gavin / Elena — thanks for the redlines and for the call earlier today. Attached is a proposed middle-ground from our legal team (Proposed_Press_Clause_redline.docx) that: 

- Narrows the logo license to approved assets and a limited set of placements, with a 14-business-day approval SLA on Redwood for approvals.
- Allows mutual sign-off on press; proposes 14/30 day windows depending on announcement size as a compromise.
- Permits anonymized case studies and aggregated metrics if logo use is denied.

Marissa has a campaign scheduled for the week of July 9; to hit that date we need a firm yes/no by June 26. If ClarSky can agree to the 14-day SLA for standard press and provide a one-time pre-approved asset pack by June 26, we can proceed without escalation. If not, please let us know and we'll raise to our VP of Sales to request a limited exception that guarantees a priority review lane for your launches.

Next steps: see attached proposed clause. If you can reply with a one-line acceptance or markups, we will incorporate into the MSA and proceed to finalize the order form and DocuSign flow.

Thanks again — looking forward to closing this out.

Soojin Lee
